podcast.title: British Indie Label
podcast.body: A UK indie label that was a major factor in breaking new music, particularly since the punk era of the 1970s. "There was rough trade, two-tone and stiff, mute, and dozens of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Culturally Significant Label
podcast.body: Established by Jerry Dammers of The Specials, Two-tone evolved beyond just a record label to become a distinct sound and a cultural movement, actively promoting racial harmony. Its first release, "Gangsters" by The Specials in May 1979, sold 5,000 copies and reached number six on the British charts, an unprecedented success for an indie record. "So he started his own label and he called it Two-tone. This became not just a record label, but a sound and a cultural movement promoting racial harmony."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Financial Collapse
podcast.body: Two-Tone Records, like other British indie labels of the 1980s, struggled with financial management and eventually "sink under the weight of its debt," indicating a common problem of poor business practices within the scene. "two-tone would sink under the weight of its debt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Financial Troubles
podcast.body: Towards the end of the second wave, Two Tone started experiencing serious money troubles, contributing to the decline of the scene. "Two Tone started having serious money troubles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founding and Ethos
podcast.body: Founded in March 1979 by Jerry Dammers of The Specials with £700 borrowed from friends and family, the label's name reflected the black and white suits worn by 1960s mods and skinheads, symbolizing the band's peaceful, multi-racial makeup. "In March 1979, the Specials borrowed 700 pounds from family and friends to form an independent record label that Jerry Damors called Two Tone. This was after the black and white suits worn by mods and skinheads in the 60s and after the peaceful, multi-racial makeup of the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Second Wave Ska Hub
podcast.body: Two Tone was an indie record label founded by Jerry Dammers, specifically created to release records by The Specials and other like-minded groups that were part of the second wave Ska revival. The label was a major force in this movement. "Jerry Damrs formed an indie record label called Two Tone to release records by the specials and other like-minded groups."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Success in Post-Punk Britain
podcast.body: Two Tone had a successful run over several years as ska became one of the biggest trends in post-punk Britain, also signing other groups like The Selector, Madness, and The Beat. "Two Tone ended up having a pretty good run over the next few years as Scott became one of the biggest trends in post-punk Britain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Specials' Debut Album
podcast.body: The Two-Tone label released The Specials' first album in 1979, which was produced by Elvis Costello. This album is credited with significantly propelling the ska revival into full swing. "Look at the credits on that first album from the Specials on the Two-Tone label who produced it, who showed this raw, untamed band from Coventry had a capture of their energy on tape."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
